title: Leonard Feather's origin of the jazz polls
summary: Ridley relays that Feather started the polls to get magazines to cover black artists, and Sam recalls poll orchestras.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Segregation on the road and the bandstand

blocks.x: Well Leonard Feather admitted to me that the whole concept of the polls in jazz was something that he instigated because when he first came to this country, he was very drugged that here was the music that he had been listening to up in England and he was very excited about it and he came over, basically came over as a band boy with Duke Ellington and he couldn't understand why there was nothing really being written about the black jazz artist and he said that he wanted to see them get more visibility so he went to this particular magazine and sold them on the idea of having a poll because it was an idea that people could relate to because it was a commercial kind of thing. And he said that that was his basic reason for starting the polls there because in order to get the magazine to write about them because they didn't particularly want to write about these black jazz artists,

they wanted to write about Red Nichols and some of them old, Jimmy Dorsey and people like that. They didn't want to write about these black jazz artists. And he said that the reason why he got the idea started was because of that reason, because it offered a thing that the magazine could relate to to stimulate their sales. But then the whole thing just got turned around, you know.
I don't know when he came to this country.
It was back in the late thirties, about 1938.
Because I remember when they used to have those poll orchestras. Remember they used to have those poll, put all the guys that won the poll together.
Yeah but he was the one that was supposed to have instigated all that stuff.
Yeah but he claims it was a gimmick so the magazine publishers would write about them and stimulate the magazine sales.
And that was the only way they'd do it.
